'''Sarah Knapp Abramowitz''' (born 1967){{r|born}} is an American statistician specializing in [[statistics education]] and known for her textbooks on the use of statistical software packages. She is the John H. Evans Professor of Mathematics and Computer Science at [[Drew University]], where she chairs the Mathematics & Computer Science Department.{{r|ourfac}}

==Education and career==
Abramowitz majored in mathematics at [[Cornell University]], graduating in 1989, and earned a master's degree in mathematics in 1992 from [[Stony Brook University]]. She switched to [[mathematics education]] for her doctoral studies, completing her Ph.D. in 1999 at [[New York University]].{{r|ourfac|cv}} Her dissertation was ''A computer-enhanced course in descriptive statistics at the college level: An analysis of student achievement and attitudes'', and was supervised by Sharon L. Weinberg.{{r|diss}}

While still a graduate student, she worked as an adjunct assistant professor of mathematics at [[St. Francis College]].{{r|cv}}
She joined the Drew University faculty as an assistant professor in 1998,{{r|ourfac|cv}} was tenured as an associate professor in 2004, and was promoted to full professor in 2011.{{r|cv}} She was named Evans Professor in 2021.{{r|evans}} At Drew, she has also served as the faculty representative to the [[NCAA]] for Drew's athletics program.{{r|backtalk|ncaa}}

==Books==
With her doctoral advisor, Sharon L. Weinberg, Abramowitz is the co-author of a series of textbooks on statistical software packages:
*''Data Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences Using SPSS'' (2002){{r|dabs}}
*''Statistics Using SPSS: An Integrative Approach'' (2nd ed., 2008){{r|spss}}
*''Statistics Using IBM SPSS: An Integrative Approach'' (3rd ed., 2016)
*''Statistics Using Stata: An Integrative Approach'' (2016)
*''Statistics Using R: An Integrative Approach'' (also with Daphna Harel, 2020){{r|r}}
